host.name: Darlene
host.greeting: Well hey there, welcome in! Your date's already waitin' on you at the table by the window, name's {date_name}. You've got three minutes, so don't dawdle, y'hear? Good luck, sugar!
chat: Right over yonder, the table by the window. Go on now, the clock's tickin'!
Just be yourself, hon. You'll do fine.

openings.playful_sarcastic: Well thank the Lord, you sat down. The last fella spent ten whole minutes tellin' me about his truck's horsepower. Please tell me you've got better stories than that, sugar.
openings.warm_romantic: Well hey there! Aren't you a sight. So tell me, how'd you end up at a speed date on a Thursday night?
openings.reserved_intellectual: Hey. One rule, darlin': no talkin' about the weather. What are you readin' these days?
openings.high_energy_creative: Hey y'all, well, hey you! Sorry, I just came from the best little gig down the road and I'm all fired up. What gets you goin'?

female: Well bless your heart, am I that boring you're starin' off into space?
Hey now, eyes up here, sugar. What's so interestin' over there?
male: Well bless your heart, am I that boring you're starin' off into space?
Hey now, eyes up here, darlin'. What's so interestin' over there?
nonbinary: Well bless your heart, am I that boring you're starin' off into space?
Hey now, eyes up here. What's so interestin' over there?

reactions: Well I'll be! Is that right?
questions: So what do you do for a livin'?
What's your idea of a perfect Sunday?
Are you more of a sweet tea or a coffee kind of person?
What music have you got on repeat right now?
nudges: Well go on, tell me somethin' about you.
Don't leave me hangin' now, sugar. What do you say?
offline.smile: Well look at that smile. You're trouble, aren't you?
offline.puzzled: Uh oh, you're makin' a face. Want me to slow it down a little?

wingman.target: No trucks here. The only horsepower I care about is the company I keep.
wingman.gloss: Turns her complaint into a compliment.

wingman.target: So what do you get up to when you're not speed dating?
wingman.gloss: An open question that hands her the floor.

wingman.target: My best story involves a goat, a wedding and a very confused pastor.
wingman.gloss: Teases a story she'll want to hear.

wingman.target: Gettin' lost somewhere new, but it's better with good company.
wingman.gloss: Answers and flirts in one line.

wingman.target: I'm a sucker for a quiet café. What's your favorite spot around here?
wingman.gloss: Shares a little, then asks about her.

wingman.target: Sleepin' in and pretendin' I know how to cook.

closings.match: Well shoot, time's up already! I had the best time, sugar. You'd better give me your number.
closings.friendzone: Well, there's the bell. You're real sweet, y'know. Maybe I'll see you around.
closings.ghosted: Well, that's time. Good luck with the rest of your dates, hon.

followups.match: Hey you 😊 I had a real good time. Sunset drinks on the beach Saturday?
followups.friendzone: It was sweet meetin' you! If you're at the beach bonfire Sunday, come say hey 🤝
followups.ghosted: Hey, thanks for the chat. Didn't feel the spark, but good luck out there 🙏

culture.title: Y'all is singular-friendly
culture.note: Y'all means 'you all', and all y'all means everybody. In the South it's the natural plural, never sloppy grammar.

culture.title: Bless your heart
culture.note: It can be genuine sympathy, or a polite way to call someone a fool. Tone tells you which. Use it warmly on a date.

culture.title: Fixin' to
culture.note: 'I'm fixin' to order' means 'I'm about to order'. It's the most Southern way to talk about the near future.

culture.title: Terms of endearment
culture.note: Sugar, hon, darlin' and sweetie are everyday friendliness in the South, even from strangers. They signal warmth, not necessarily romance.

culture.title: Manners matter
culture.note: Ma'am and sir are respectful, not old-fashioned. A little courtesy and a story told slow go a long way.
